headline: Advance Reservation for Backcountry Water Access Sites
reservation: Access to this semi-wilderness park requires a valid backcountry permit for designated sites, distinct from any local cottage rentals. Reservations must be secured through the Ontario Parks online system, as there is no central gatehouse for walk-in transactions. Policies for vehicle parking at specific access points like Anstruther Lake or Long Lake are subject to change and must be verified via official park channels.

days.title: Anstruther Lake Waters

stops.name: Anstruther Lake Access
stops.detail: The primary launch point for exploring the park's central interior, providing access to sprawling granite shorelines.

stops.name: Rathbun Lake Portage
stops.detail: A manageable transition for paddlers looking to reach the quieter, more secluded northern reaches of the park.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes to access points; road conditions vary by season.
days.note: Wind conditions on larger lakes can significantly impact paddle times; check local forecasts.

days.title: Coon Lake Exploration

stops.name: Coon Lake Access Point

stops.name: Bottle Lake Route

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Apsley; gravel roads may be narrow.
days.note: Paddling is the primary mode of travel; land-based hiking is limited to specific rugged corridors.

days.title: Mississagua River Corridors

stops.name: Mississagua Lake Launch
stops.detail: A gateway to the interconnected water systems that define the western park boundary.

stops.name: Gold Lake Passage
stops.detail: Navigate through narrow channels that showcase the park's significant biological diversity.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; access involves forest service roads.
days.note: Water levels in river sections fluctuate; check with Ontario Parks regarding spring run-off or autumn lows.

intel.title: Access Point Constraints
intel.text: Parking is limited to designated gravel lots at official access points like Long Lake. Spaces are not guaranteed during peak summer weekends; avoid parking on narrow shoulders to prevent towing.

intel.title: Backcountry Communication
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly unreliable once you move away from Highway 28. Plan for a complete lack of data services in the interior lake basins.

intel.title: Apsley Supply Hub
intel.text: Apsley serves as the final reliable location for fuel and basic provisions before entering the park interior. There are no services available once you depart the main regional roads.

intel.title: Paddling Pace
intel.text: Suggested departure times allow for manageable portages before midday winds rise. Early starts are recommended for those traversing multiple lake chains.

intel.title: Water Entry Only
intel.text: Most sites are inaccessible by foot; a canoe or kayak is mandatory for backcountry travel. Ensure your vessel meets local safety requirements before launching.

plan.arrival: Collect supplies in Peterborough or Apsley before heading to your specific lake access point. Check in with the digital permit system prior to arrival as on-site staff presence is minimal.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are generally sufficient for the main access roads, though high-clearance is beneficial for secondary forest routes.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset over Long Lake offers classic Shield silhouettes, depending on cloud cover and seasonal smoke.
